stories.new_fact: AP obtained three subpoenas sent October 21 and 24 requiring Los Angeles County election employees to appear November 4 and seeking election-record material.
stories.new_takeaway: A compulsory-records demand creates preservation and legal-response work but does not itself change a voter procedure or establish an election-law violation.
stories.why_now: The subpoenas and the reported court date became public October 29.
stories.previous_coverage: The prior seven episodes covered Ohio campaign and election-administration context, not this California federal-subpoena escalation.
stories.uncertainty: The public subpoenas do not establish the outcome of the investigation, a court ruling on scope, or a change in ballot handling.
stories.watch: November 4 appearances and any court filing that states the legal theory or limits scope.

stories.new_fact: Wendy’s confirmed receipt of a nonbinding $7.35-per-share cash proposal, about $1.4 billion, and formed an independent committee to evaluate it.
stories.new_takeaway: For Central Ohio the operational fact is a board review at a Dublin headquarters, not a completed transaction or evidence of job, store, supplier, or price changes.
stories.why_now: The proposal and committee confirmation were reported October 28.
stories.previous_coverage: No Wendy’s ownership proposal appeared in the seven scripts compared.
stories.uncertainty: The committee may reject, negotiate, or pursue another option; no completed transaction has been announced.
stories.watch: A company filing, committee communication, or quarterly result with a revised operating plan.

stories.new_fact: Freddie Mac auctioned 25 deeply delinquent first-lien residential loans with $3.8 million unpaid principal balance, serviced by Selene Finance, with December settlement expected.
stories.new_takeaway: A small pool sale is a servicing-transfer and borrower-communication workflow whose protection depends on carrying forward agreements and pending loss-mitigation actions, not a new national borrower-eligibility rule.
stories.why_now: Freddie Mac published the transaction October 28.
stories.previous_coverage: October 29 mentioned the auction and Freddie Score data; this script takes the distinct operational handoff and borrower-protection takeaway rather than repeating a market-size conclusion.
stories.uncertainty: The release does not establish national delinquency direction, post-sale borrower outcomes, or a change in loss-mitigation policy.
stories.watch: Expected December settlement and any later disclosure of servicing or borrower outcomes.

stories.new_fact: Napier AI announced completed technology validation for integration of LSEG World-Check On Demand into its Transaction Screening product for risk-based payment screening.
stories.new_takeaway: A validated data integration is a vendor capability change, not evidence of a bank production outcome; alert quality, misses, and manual workload still require a local comparison.
stories.why_now: Napier published the integration announcement October 29.
stories.previous_coverage: The seven prior scripts covered bank service metrics, agent controls, and announced access changes, not this payment-screening integration.
stories.uncertainty: No named customer, deployment volume, alert baseline, false-positive rate, missed-match rate, payment-delay result, or independent test is disclosed.
stories.watch: Named financial-institution deployment or a before-and-after screening-quality result.
stories.ledger_row_changed: Napier AI / LSEG, lane 2: added a new announced payment-screening integration row; vendor claim, technology validation only, no bank production outcome disclosed.

stories.new_fact: OpenAI released GPT-6 Luna (October 29), reporting changed safety-evaluation results, including 99.91 percent instruction-hierarchy robustness and differing HealthBench results against the October 7 version.
stories.new_takeaway: Version-specific lab evaluations can improve in one safety dimension and move lower in another task, so an enterprise must test its own bounded workflow rather than use a single headline score.
stories.why_now: The safety addendum and version update are dated October 29.
stories.previous_coverage: The prior seven scripts discussed GPT-6.1 Terra, Decisions API, and other access changes, not this Luna version-specific safety evaluation.
stories.uncertainty: All quoted results are OpenAI-reported evaluations rather than independent replication or regulated-workflow evidence.
stories.watch: Independent replication or a version-specific task evaluation with error, citation, and correction measures.

The October 29 prior episode mentioned the Freddie sale; today uses a new, source-specific servicer-boarding and agreement-continuity takeaway rather than rerunning the prior capital-markets framing. Every full segment was checked for changed fact and takeaway against the seven scripts.
